text: National University of Computer & Emerging Sciences - NUCES - Karachi Department of Artificial Intelligence 6.1.1.4 The solution: Homogenous Coordinates Homogeneous coordinates bypass the origin limitation by adding a temporary, dummy "1" to standard 2D coordinates, turning (x, y) into (x, y, 1). This mathematical trick allows computers to perform translations using only matrix multiplication, completely eliminating the need for a separate vector addition step. The Problem with Vector Addition The standard affine equation is p' = Ap + b This forces the computer to perform a matrix multiplication (Ap) for scaling or rotating, stop that process, and then perform a separate vector addition (+b) to slide the object. Graphics processors (GPUs) are deeply optimized to execute continuous, uninterrupted chains of matrix multiplications. Breaking that hardware pipeline to switch to vector addition creates a massive computational bottleneck when calculating millions of coordinate points per second. The Matrix Multiplication Solution By upgrading the math to a 3 x 3 matrix, we can fold the translation values tx and ty directly into the rightmost column: 10 tx X 01 tyy 0011 When the computer executes this multiplication, the row-by-column math forces the "1" in the coordinate vector to multiply against the tx and ty in the matrix. These cleanly outputs the exact translation equations algebraically : FAST NUCES - Karachi Talha Shahid 16
